title: crypto2dev_hmac Final: HMAC ctx freed on success path even when op_fd acquire fails
description: In crypto2dev_hmac() Final branch: 'op_fd = crypto2dev_pool_acquire(); if (op_fd < 0) return WC_HW_E;' returns immediately without freeing hmac->devCtx or clearing the pointer. wc_HmacFree() (wolfcrypt/src/hmac.c:1438) then sees 'devId \!= INVALID_DEVID && devCtx \!= NULL' and calls wc_CryptoCb_Hmac(hmac, type, NULL, 0, finalHash) — which again enters the Final branch in crypto2dev_hmac() (digest=finalHash \!= NULL). If pool_acquire now succeeds, the HMAC is silently completed in wc_HmacFree(), and the MAC bytes are written to a stack buffer inside wc_HmacFree() that is immediately discarded. If pool_acquire fails again, we get infinite recursion risk... actually not infinite because wc_HmacFree is only called once and the return of crypto2dev_hmac is ignored. The real harm: the HmacCtx struct and its accumulated data buffer are leaked unless wc_HmacFree is called — and when it is called, the accumulated plaintext input is silently processed by the hardware and the result discarded. The fix: on the 'op_fd < 0' early return in the Final path, free the ctx and null devCtx so wc_HmacFree has nothing to clean up.
